median_clinician_comparator.reason: Median clinician performance may replicate suboptimal care at scale without ensuring patient benefit
Median clinician standard anchors the bar to practice variation, so poor practice licenses poor devices
A model's miss repeats across every patient, so median clinician performance does not mean median risk
Median generalist performance should not define acceptable safety for specialty tasks
A median clinician comparator would normalize existing gaps in care as an acceptable ceiling
Specialist-level tools should be benchmarked against specialists, not generalists or a median clinician
median_clinician_comparator.alternative: Board-certified specialists in the relevant field

voluntary_model_files.reason: Foundation model developers have strong competitive incentives to withhold provenance, architecture, and failure mode information
Voluntary files draw disclosure only from developers with little to hide
Hosted models change every few minutes, so no master file can stay current
Model developers have limited commercial incentive to disclose safety-relevant limitations of their models
Foundation model developers have no incentive to participate in a voluntary program
A voluntary file cannot replace binding change notice when developers lack incentive to disclose
voluntary_model_files.alternative: Binding change-notification obligation with a predefined response protocol

patient_facing_risk.reason: Patient-facing status should not automatically raise risk on the consequences axis
What distinguishes risk is whether the user can realistically verify output at the moment of reliance
Patient-facing use should not by itself create a presumption of higher risk
FDA should not presume that patients lack domain knowledge and HCPs possess it
Regulatory burden should scale with clinical consequence, not with whether the user is a patient
Patient-facing versus HCP-facing status should not serve as a categorical proxy for risk
FDA should not assume patients cannot handle clinical information
Patient information chatbots resemble libraries and should not be restricted like medical devices.

directiveness_continuum.reason: Directive outputs are medical advice, so outputs not approved by FDA must be labeled for information only
Wording and tone are hard to define and manufacturers can change wording without changing function
In their record, directiveness was not a property of the function, so it cannot modify intended use
Functions should be classified by what their output asserts, not how it is worded
An axis based on output wording can be moved by rewording without changing user options

third_party.reason: A third-party requirement invites organizations to game the system and profit from prolonged testing
Requiring the benchmark itself to be independent would leave small developers with no benchmark

risk_framework.reason: Device activity does not equal probability of harm, so the two axes are insufficient
The two axes are too simple for real-world use and ignore population-level harm
risk_framework.alternative: Tiered risk categories modeled on the EU AI Act

escalation_errors.reason: For protocol delivery, escalation is a protocol step, not a trade-off between two error rates

postmarket_tradeoff.reason: Postmarket review is not enough for a new technology with many unknowns
Accepting premarket uncertainty transfers risk from the sponsor who chose to deploy to patients who did not
Postmarket monitoring must supplement strong premarket evidence so patients are not test subjects
Postmarket monitoring should verify premarket claims, not substitute for inadequate premarket evidence
Reduced premarket evidence moves discovery of uncertainty onto patients through harm
Uncertainty shifting should stay case by case under existing guidance, not apply to GenAI as a class
postmarket_tradeoff.alternative: Existing case-level uncertainty guidance with a preauthorized active data-collection plan

flexible_change_control.reason: A PCCP is the wrong instrument for changes the sponsor cannot predetermine
Changes an AI directs to itself, with scope not describable in advance, should not be preapproved
flexible_change_control.alternative: Record, re-benchmark, and require named human sign-off for every self-proposed change

no_care_comparator.reason: Comparing against understaffed care can make a product appear beneficial
An unavailable alternative changes a device's benefit, not the consequence of its errors
Access constraints should not justify unreviewed AI reads; no interpretation is not the only alternative
no_care_comparator.alternative: Use standard-of-care comparators such as specialist review of images

confirmation_flex.reason: Prospective clinical studies should be the main way to establish safety for devices influencing patient care
Requires real-world clinical implementation evidence; reader studies and controlled tests are insufficient.

competency_eval.reason: A device that bounds its inputs, outputs, and output variability should be evaluable by established methods

Personal grievance about alleged fraud, paternity orders, and loss of control over identity and records
Patients must give informed consent before voice prints are released and used to train AI
Add evidence quality calibration to the evaluation of generative AI medical devices
Audit whether clinician responses to AI outputs led to model changes, delivery changes, or dismissal
Medical AI should evaluate complementary and traditional treatments by the same standards as conventional ones
Clarify what counts as generative AI and consider a parallel proposal for causal AI
Treat where the output appears in the clinician workflow as part of the device being evaluated
Clarify the boundary between AI that conveys a clinician's plan and AI exercising independent judgment
Attachment reproduces FDA's discussion paper with no added commentary
Safe implementation of generative AI medical devices is a shared human responsibility
Keep responsibility for model validity, drift, and monitoring with model makers, not pathology labs
Consider standardized, machine checkable minimum documentation for datasets used in benchmarking and clinical confirmation
Recognize local version locking of models as an acceptable risk mitigation for change control
Assess whether evaluation and monitoring layers provide truly independent evidence about device failure
Accuracy, bias, and privacy risks of generative AI outweigh its benefits
Postmarket surveillance should involve all stakeholders and preserve full interaction logs for incident investigation
Self-changing AI should not enter practice until point-of-care verification and validation is solved
Nurses should be involved in AI evaluation and postmarket monitoring, with near misses tracked
Nurses must be included in discussions on regulating generative AI devices

AI needs constant human correction, lacks context, and cannot replace human relationships
AI tools in nursing practice sometimes write confusing or nonsensical output
Track whether AI alerts reach clinicians and link them to patient outcomes
GenAI device guidance should connect to section 524B cybersecurity duties for foundation models
AI scribes are about 70% accurate and call-center triage bots lack FDA oversight
Nurses' concerns should be heard when monitoring AI tools
Federal leadership should set common standards and datasets that states accept
Wants CRNAs recognized as qualified clinicians, comparators, and partners in postmarket monitoring

open_questions.question: Should patient-facing use raise a device's risk level?

sides.label: Yes, in some cases or with safeguards
No, risk depends on whether users can check the output

open_questions.question: Can voluntary disclosure from model developers give FDA what it needs?

sides.label: Yes, if the device maker stays responsible for safety
No, disclosure should be required or the evidence burden raised

open_questions.question: How far can postmarket monitoring stand in for premarket evidence?

sides.label: Only if monitoring is shown to catch failures before harm

open_questions.question: Should directiveness be judged by an output's wording or by its effect?

sides.label: By degree, including wording, specificity, and context
By what the output claims or does, since wording is easy to change
